newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa wipes out losses, ends firmer on stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa wipes out losses, ends firmer on stg.

text.p: Currency-related trade reigned over LIFFE cocoa on Monday as prices recouped earlier losses after sterling eased from fresh highs against the dollar.
Traders noted remarks by the Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze who said in Gabon that the new cocoa season would begin in the next two to three days.

Uncertainty over the new arrivals while farm-gate and freight rates have yet to be fixed had created suspense among traders, already jittery about the potentially large crop for a second consecutive year.
Gauze pegged the Ivorian crop at between 900,000 and 950,000 tonnes, a level considerably lower than trade estimates.
"I don't think one should pay too much attention to that," said one trader.
The late session hosted a small dose of trade buying and short covering, pulling the benchmark second-month March contract to a finish of 986 stg a tonne, up one on the day.
Earlier it nudged the bottom end of its current range, narrowly escaping a test of the critical 975 support.
Much of the selling was linked to long liquidation after disappointment over Friday's sharp losses despite a healthy rise in the U.S. third quarter grind.
Traders said the Ivorian season could kick off with a good volume this year, blended with left-overs of last season's mid-crop.
Turnover on the Exchange totalled 4,532 lots, mainly clustered in nearby positions with interest in forwards sagging.
Producer country ministers started talks in Gabon on Monday to discuss output strategy after cuts agreed under the umbrella of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) in September.
A decision is expected on Wednesday.
Technically, March is haunted by the September low of 975 stg, failure of which to hold will herald steeper losses toward lows last seen in March.
